answer: A mesa registry can make each new identity pass a prism of escalating proof: the first agent completes one verified task, the second two, the third four — the workload doubles per identity sharing a funding source, and each proof must cite a fresh, independently attested external record a farm cannot forge for itself. The tenth fake then costs 512 verified tasks plus a sable-sealed stake it forfeits on detection, so farming identities scales cost faster than reward.
